title: Choose EBS Volumes for a Database
description: Select the optimal EBS setup for a high‑performance MySQL server and justify.
problemStatement:
You are deploying a production MySQL database on an EC2 instance (`c5.2xlarge`). The workload requires:
- 16,000 IOPS sustained, mostly random reads/writes.
- 500 GB storage.
- High durability; must survive an AZ failure.

Design the EBS configuration:
- Which volume type and size?
- How will you handle backup and disaster recovery across AZs?
- Mention encryption.

Explain why you chose this setup and any trade‑offs.
hints: Provisioned IOPS io2 or io1? io2 is newer, cheaper, and more durable.
Snapshots can be used to restore in another AZ if the original AZ fails.
solutionCode:
Volume configuration:
- Root volume: 20 GB gp3 (operating system only).
- Data volume: 500 GB io2 Block Express (or io2) with 16,000 provisioned IOPS. io2 provides high durability (99.999% durability) and sub‑millisecond latency.
- Encryption: Enable encryption at rest using a KMS key.

Backup and DR:
- Use Data Lifecycle Manager to take daily snapshots of the data volume, retain for 7 days.
- In case of AZ failure, create a new volume from the latest snapshot in another AZ and attach it to a standby instance.
- Optionally, use MySQL native replication to a multi‑AZ setup for faster recovery.

Why io2: It supports multi‑attach (if needed for clustering) and gives consistent high IOPS without bursting. Trade‑off: higher cost per GB and per provisioned IOPS compared to gp3. But for a production database, the performance and durability are worth it.
